title: McKay v. Central Indiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC held the complaint administratively out of order under BCO 43-3 because the e-mail/correspondence sent by complainant to the lower court clerk was insufficient to constitute proper notice. The SJC reached no merits issue and granted no other relief.
first_summary: The SJC found McKay's complaint against Central Indiana Presbytery administratively out of order because an e-mail to the lower court clerk did not meet BCO 43-3 notice requirements. No merits determination was made. All participating commissioners concurred.
summary: The SJC held that TE David McKay's complaint against Central Indiana Presbytery was administratively out of order. The decisive defect was procedural: the e-mail transmitted to the lower court clerk did not satisfy BCO 43-3 because the complainant's correspondence was insufficient to constitute proper notice. The SJC therefore reached no merits issue. All 24 participating commissioners concurred, with no dissent. The ruling enforces BCO 43-3's notice requirement before a complaint can proceed.
